author: ValWood
body:
Apologies, when I reviewed the cargo receptors in my models, this was the wrong way around. 

Erv46 (along with erv41) is a reterograde  cargo adaptor.

Therefore GO:0006890 | retrograde vesicle-mediated transport, Golgi to endoplasmic reticulum
should be reinstated and  
GO:0006888 | endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport | IBA with S000000040 , Q9Y282 , S000004532 , PTN000862199 , Q969X5 , Q96RQ1
should be removed.

[The Erv41-Erv46 complex serves as a retrograde receptor to retrieve misfolded secretory proteins that have escaped from the ER.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40327065/)
Fuesler JA, Blais JR, Barlowe C.
Mol Biol Cell. 2025 Jul 1;36(7):ar80. doi: 10.1091/mbc.E25-02-0090. Epub 2025 May 6.
PMID: 40327065

PMID: 25583996 
PMID: 31825724

thanks, did you block "GO:0006888 | endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport |"
the confusion arose because this cargo adaptor travels out in the anterograde direction even though it is only used in the reterrograde direction

author: ValWood
body:
Hi Ruth!

Q9Y282 ERGIC3  endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport (Complex Portal)
Q969X5 ERGIC1 endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport (HGNC)
Q96RQ1 ERGIC2  endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport (Complex Portal)


Allthough there is information that these were involved in anterograde transport, the current thinking appears to have moved.

This is a Claude summary

 The core logic is:
The best-characterized function of Erv41–Erv46 is retrograde retrieval — grabbing escaped ER-resident proteins from the Golgi and sending them back. The pH-dependent binding (binds at acidic Golgi pH, releases at neutral ER pH) is mechanistically tailored for retrograde capture. The direct binding data from the Barlowe lab maps specifically to this retrieval function.
So when you knock out ERGIC2/3 and see anterograde transport defects (Cx43 stuck in the ER, reduced α1-antitrypsin secretion), one parsimonious explanation is exactly what you're suggesting: the ER export machinery itself depends on components that are recycled back via ERGIC2/3. If COPII coat subunits, cargo receptors, SNAREs, or other cycling factors aren't being properly retrieved, the anterograde pathway degrades secondarily. The ER gradually loses the machinery it needs to export anything efficiently.
This would also explain why the effects are selective rather than global — only cargo that depends on limiting or specific recycled components would be affected, while bulk flow secretion remains largely intact (which is what's observed in both yeast and mammalian knockouts).
It's worth noting that the Barlowe lab's finding that only ~20 out of ~3,500 proteins were affected in erv41Δ/erv46Δ yeast fits either model — direct receptor for a small cargo set, or indirect effects on a subset of trafficking-sensitive clients. And the fact that Cx36 is completely unaffected while Cx43 is impaired suggests the "anterograde cargo receptor" model has specificity problems that your indirect-recycling model handles more gracefully.
The one piece of evidence that's harder to explain with the pure indirect model is the co-IP data showing physical association between ERGIC2/3 and connexins — but as the research noted, co-IP doesn't distinguish direct binding from being in the same complex or even the same vesicle.


I guess you could keep the original annotations, although they are now looking like they could be phenotypes based on  disrupting the supply of anterograde transport components, this isn't conclusive. However, I  would definitely not propagate based on the current opinion.
I have also contacted the Barlow lab to check this interpretation (they have done most of the work on this complex, and their recent few papers , see above, refer only  to the retrograde role).

author: ValWood
body:
Author agreed, although there is not complete agreement. 
So it could be but the current evidence  "However, the accumulation secretory cargo in the ER could be due to reduced levels of ER chaperones that are normally retrieved by Erv41-Erv46."
So I think we should not make that annotation with only a phenotype and annotate only to retrograde unless there is an assay identifying a specific cargo (not just co-IP)
